s: The disease Minamata is associated with which pollutant and country-year combination?
x: Minamata disease was caused by methyl mercury contamination in Japan and was identified in 1956.
tq: Use the disease–pollutant–location–year association.

s: Which one of the following correctly explains the principal environmental pathway involved in Minamata disease?
o: Nitrate reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of infant blood
Cadmium accumulates in bones through contaminated irrigation water
Methyl mercury biomagnifies through fish and causes neurological damage
x: Methyl mercury biomagnified in fish and caused neurological damage in Minamata disease. The other options describe fluorosis, blue baby syndrome and Itai-itai disease respectively.
tq: Match the mechanism to the disease rather than relying only on the disease name.

s:
Consider the following statements about fluorosis:
1. Dental fluorosis mainly affects children below eight years of age.
2. Knock-knee is a form of skeletal fluorosis.
3. Fluorosis may also have non-skeletal manifestations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Dental fluorosis is associated particularly with children under eight, knock-knee is skeletal fluorosis, and fluorosis also has non-skeletal forms.
tq: Check each statement against the classification of fluorosis.

s: Fluoride causes fluorosis principally by replacing which component in hydroxyapatite?
x: Fluoride replaces hydroxyl in hydroxyapatite and forms fluorapatite.
tq: Test the precise biochemical substitution rather than the broader disease association.

s: Which of the following combinations relating to fluoride standards and observance is correct?
o: WHO guideline: 0.5 mg/L; BIS acceptable limit: 1.0 mg/L; National Fluorosis Day: 5 June
WHO guideline: 1.0 mg/L; BIS acceptable limit: 1.5 mg/L; National Fluorosis Day: 9 September
WHO guideline: 1.5 mg/L; BIS acceptable limit: 1.0 mg/L; National Fluorosis Day: 9 September
WHO guideline: 1.5 mg/L; BIS acceptable limit: 1.5 mg/L; National Fluorosis Day: 13 September
x: The WHO limit is 1.5 mg/L, while the BIS acceptable limit is 1.0 mg/L; the permissible BIS limit is 1.5 mg/L. National Fluorosis Day is observed on 9 September.
tq: Split the option into linked numerical and date components.

s: The Nalgonda technique for defluoridation uses which combination of materials?
x: The Nalgonda technique uses alum, lime and bleaching powder to remove excess fluoride from water.
tq: Recall the specific treatment-material combination.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Arsenicosis — skin lesions and skin and lung cancer
Blue baby syndrome — methyl mercury biomagnification
x: Arsenicosis or blackfoot disease is associated with skin lesions and skin and lung cancer. The other pairings interchange the pollutants and diseases.
tq: Find the correctly matched disease–pollutant effect pair among confusable associations.

s: The blue baby syndrome associated with nitrate contamination is medically known as
x: Excess nitrate in drinking water can cause methaemoglobinaemia, commonly called blue baby syndrome, in infants.
tq: Discriminate between the common name and the medical term.

s:
Arrange the following developments in the Ganga conservation framework in chronological order:
A. National Ganga Council replaced NGRBA
B. Central Ganga Authority and GAP-I
C. NGRBA was constituted
D. NMCG was set up as the implementing arm of NGRBA
x: The sequence is 1985 Central Ganga Authority and GAP-I, 2009 NGRBA, 2011 NMCG, and 2016 National Ganga Council.
tq: Place the dated institutional milestones first and last before resolving the middle sequence.

s: Ganga Action Plan-II, launched in 1993, covered which group of rivers?
x: GAP-II covered the Yamuna, Gomti, Damodar and Mahananda rivers.
tq: Recall the exact river-group membership.

s: Which of the following statements about the institutional history of Ganga conservation is correct?
o: The NRCP was created in 1985 and GAP-I was merged into it in 1995.
The NGRBA was chaired by the Prime Minister and was replaced by the National Ganga Council in 2016.
The NMCG replaced the National Ganga Council in 2011.
The Central Ganga Authority was established in 2016 as a registered society.
x: NGRBA, chaired by the Prime Minister, was replaced by the National Ganga Council in 2016. NMCG was set up in 2011 as a registered society and implementing arm of NGRBA.
tq: Use the authority–chairperson–replacement relationship to reject swapped institutional roles.

s: The National River Conservation Plan and Ganga Action Plan-II became linked in 1995 because
o: NRCP was merged into the National Ganga Council
GAP-II was merged into the NRCP
x: In 1995, GAP-II was merged into the National River Conservation Plan.
tq: Test the direction of institutional merger, a common APPSC trap.

s: The Namami Gange Mission was announced in 2014–15 with an outlay of ₹20,000 crore for
x: The original Namami Gange Mission had an outlay of ₹20,000 crore for five years, covering 2015–2020.
tq: Separate the original mission period from the later Phase-II period.

s: Namami Gange Mission is identified as a key policy priority towards achieving which Sustainable Development Goal?
x: Namami Gange is linked with SDG 6, which concerns clean water and sanitation.
tq: Match the programme objective with the correct SDG.

s: Namami Gange-II was approved in 2022 with an outlay of ₹22,500 crore for the period
x: Namami Gange-II was approved in 2022 with ₹22,500 crore for 2021–2026, up to 31 March 2026.
tq: Distinguish the Phase-II dates and outlay from the original mission figures.

s: Which of the following pairs represents the twin goals of the Namami Gange Mission?
x: Nirmal Dhara denotes unpolluted flow, while Aviral Dhara denotes continuous flow.
tq: Distinguish the formal twin-goal terminology from related programme components.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Namami Gange Mission:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
2. It has received support from the World Bank.
3. Arth Ganga links livelihoods with the river.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Namami Gange is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti, has World Bank support, and Arth Ganga concerns river-linked livelihoods.
tq: Verify each institutional, financial and conceptual feature separately.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a component or associated activity of the Namami Gange Mission?
o: Expansion of uranium mining along the river basin
x: Sewerage, river-surface cleaning, afforestation, biodiversity, riverfront development, industrial effluent monitoring, Ganga Gram and public awareness are associated with the mission; uranium mining is not.
tq: Find the option outside the established programme-pillars group.

s: Which of the following outcomes is associated with the Namami Gange Mission?
o: A first dolphin estimate of 627 animals in March 2025
x: The reported outcomes include afforestation over 33,024 hectares. The programme also ranched 143.8 lakh carp fingerlings and estimated 6,327 dolphins in March 2025.
tq: Separate similarly presented outcome figures and units.

s: The first estimate of the Ganga river dolphin under the reported Namami Gange outcomes recorded how many dolphins in March 2025?
x: The first dolphin estimate recorded 6,327 dolphins in March 2025.
tq: Read the exact figure carefully when options contain digit transpositions.

s: The dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration generally associated with clean water is
x: A clean-water DO value is greater than 8.0 mg/L.
tq: Match the parameter with its indicative clean-water range.

s: Which parameter measures the oxygen required by bacteria to decompose organic matter?
x: Biochemical oxygen demand, or BOD, measures the oxygen needed by bacteria to decompose organic matter.
tq: Separate BOD from COD and physical water-quality measures.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. COD includes oxygen needed to oxidise biodegradable and non-biodegradable organic matter.
2. A clean-water COD value is generally less than 5.0 mg/L.
3. BOD and COD have identical meanings and measure only biodegradable matter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: COD covers biodegradable as well as non-biodegradable organic matter and its clean-water value is below 5.0 mg/L. Statement 3 is false because it incorrectly equates COD with BOD and excludes non-biodegradable matter.
tq: Use the biodegradable versus total oxidisable matter distinction.

s: A river stretch is classified as polluted when its BOD is
x: A river is considered polluted when BOD exceeds 3 mg/L; a Priority-I stretch has BOD above 30 mg/L.
tq: Distinguish the general pollution threshold from the Priority-I threshold.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between suspended solids and dissolved solids in water analysis?
o: Suspended solids are retained on a filter, whereas dissolved salts pass through it.
Suspended solids pass through a filter, whereas dissolved salts are retained.
Both suspended and dissolved solids are retained on a filter.
Neither category is affected by filtration.
x: Suspended solids such as silt and clay are retained on a filter, while dissolved solids such as sodium salts pass through it.
tq: Use the filtration distinction to separate physical categories.

s: Which one of the following sets contains only correct water-quality associations?
o: NTU—turbidity; TDS—dissolved salts; coliform count—faecal contamination
x: NTU is used for turbidity, TDS represents dissolved salts, and coliform count indicates faecal contamination.
tq: Start with the sure measurement unit and eliminate mismatched parameters.

s: For CPCB Class A water, namely a drinking-water source requiring disinfection but not conventional treatment, the total coliform limit is
x: The CPCB Class A standard specifies total coliform not exceeding 50 MPN/100 ml.
tq: Distinguish the Class A total-coliform value from the bathing faecal-coliform value.

s: The bathing-water standard cited for faecal coliform in the Ganga is
x: The cited Ganga bathing standard for faecal coliform is 2,500 MPN/100 ml.
tq: Compare the bathing standard with the stricter drinking-source standard.

s: Which sequence correctly represents the progression of trophic states in a water body?
x: The progression is oligotrophic, mesotrophic, eutrophic and, where enrichment becomes extreme, hypereutrophic.
tq: Arrange the trophic stages from low to extreme nutrient enrichment.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the causal chain in eutrophication?
o: Suspended solids → fluoride formation → algal bloom → oxygen enrichment
Nutrient depletion → algal bloom → increase in dissolved oxygen → fish kills
Algal decay → nutrient removal → oxygen enrichment → hypoxia
Nutrient enrichment → algal bloom → decomposition → depletion of dissolved oxygen
x: Nitrogen and phosphorus enrichment promotes algal blooms; decomposition of the algae consumes dissolved oxygen, causing hypoxia and fish kills.
tq: Follow the process chain from trigger to ecological consequence.

s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a trigger of eutrophication?
x: Fertiliser runoff, sewage, detergents, aquaculture effluent and airborne nitrogen can trigger eutrophication. Reduction of atmospheric nitrogen inputs is not a trigger.
tq: Find the reversed or negative form of a recognised causal factor.

s: Ritual offerings containing dairy effluent can accelerate water-quality deterioration because they may
o: Remove nitrogen and phosphorus from the water
Have high BOD and rapidly deplete dissolved oxygen
Convert all suspended solids into dissolved salts
x: Dairy effluent associated with ritual offerings can have BOD far above sewage, causing rapid depletion of dissolved oxygen.
tq: Apply the BOD–DO relationship to a specific pollution source.

s: The National River Conservation Plan (NRCP), launched in 1995, primarily aims to improve the water quality of which of the following?
o: Rivers other than the Ganga and its tributaries
The Ganga and all its tributaries only
Inter-State rivers exclusively through private funding
x: NRCP was launched in 1995 to improve the water quality of rivers other than the Ganga and its tributaries through a Centre-State cost-sharing Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
tq: Distinguish the scope of closely related river-conservation programmes.

s: Which of the following activities is supported under the National River Conservation Plan?
o: Interception and diversion of sewage, sewage treatment plants and low-cost sanitation
Construction of dams exclusively for hydropower generation
Replacement of all municipal water-supply pipelines
x: NRCP funds interception and diversion of sewage, sewage treatment plants and low-cost sanitation measures to reduce pollution loads in rivers.
tq: Identify the actual functions of the concerned programme rather than its neighbouring sectors.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National River Conservation Plan:
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme involving Centre-State cost sharing.
2. It covers 38 rivers in 16 States.
3. Godavari and Krishna are among the rivers included under it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. NRCP is a Centre-State cost-sharing scheme covering 38 rivers in 16 States, including the Godavari and Krishna.
tq: Use the coded combination to verify programme structure, coverage and examples.

s: The Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA) was launched at which event and place?
o: COP27 at Sharm el-Sheikh in November 2022
World Water Forum at New Delhi in 2023
x: GRCA was launched at COP28 held in Dubai in December 2023. It was not launched at New Delhi.
tq: Apply the event-place-year combination to avoid a location swap.

s: Which organisation leads the Global River Cities Alliance?
o: National Disaster Management Authority under the Ministry of Home Affairs
National Mission for Clean Ganga under the Ministry of Jal Shakti
NITI Aayog under the Ministry of Finance
Central Pollution Control Board under the Ministry of Environment
x: The Global River Cities Alliance is led by the National Mission for Clean Ganga under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the responsible body.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. GAP-I
b. GAP-II
c. NRCP
List-II (Year and scope)
i. 1985 — 25 main-stem Ganga towns
ii. 1993 — 60 towns on the Yamuna, Gomti, Damodar and Mahananda
iii. 1995 — rivers other than the Ganga

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: GAP-I began in 1985 for 25 main-stem Ganga towns; GAP-II began in 1993 for 60 towns on specified tributaries and rivers; NRCP began in 1995 for rivers other than the Ganga.
tq: Start from the sure year-scope pair and eliminate the remaining codes.

s:
Arrange the following programmes in chronological order of their commencement:
A. NRCP
B. GAP-II
C. GAP-I

Select the correct answer.
x: GAP-I commenced in 1985, GAP-II in 1993 and NRCP in 1995. Therefore, the correct order is C, B, A.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest years first, then place the intermediate programme.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Singtam sewerage project on the Teesta in Sikkim has a capacity of 3 MLD, not 30 MLD, and its cost is ₹39.03 crore.
tq: Find the numerical magnitude trap among closely related project details.

s: The Global River Cities Alliance covers which of the following?
o: Only cities of countries sharing the Ganga basin
Only Indian cities situated on the Ganga
Only capital cities of countries participating in COP28
River cities worldwide, with partner countries, international funding agencies and knowledge partners
x: GRCA is a global alliance covering river cities worldwide and involves partner countries, international funding agencies and knowledge partners.
tq: Reject the restrictive ‘only’ options when the programme has global coverage.

s: According to the cited CPCB report, a polluted river stretch is identified when the biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) is:
x: The cited criterion for a polluted river is BOD greater than 3 mg/L. A BOD greater than 30 mg/L identifies a Priority-I stretch.
tq: Separate the general threshold from the more severe Priority-I threshold.
sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

s: The BOD level associated with Priority-I polluted river stretches is:
x: Priority-I polluted river stretches are those with BOD greater than 30 mg/L.
tq: Test the higher category threshold rather than the ordinary pollution cut-off.
sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding polluted river stretches in India:
1. The latest cited CPCB report identified 296 polluted stretches on 271 rivers.
2. Maharashtra had the highest number of polluted stretches, with 54.
3. The number of polluted stretches increased from 351 in 2018 to 296 in the latest cited report.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the number declined from 351 in 2018 to 296 in the latest cited report.
tq: Track the direction of change instead of accepting a reversed trend.
sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

s: The number of polluted river stretches reported for 2022 was:
x: The cited series records 351 polluted stretches in 2018, 311 in 2022 and 296 in the latest report.
tq: Distinguish the year-specific intermediate figure from the latest total.
sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

s: In the water quality index cited in NITI Aayog’s Composite Water Management Index 2018, India was ranked:
x: India was ranked 120th among 122 countries in the water quality index cited in the NITI Aayog CWMI 2018.
tq: Read the rank and denominator together; do not reverse their order.
sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

s: According to the cited CGWB Annual Ground Water Quality Report, fluoride exceeded 1.5 mg/L at what percentage of the assessed sites in 2024?
x: Fluoride concentration exceeded 1.5 mg/L at 9.04% of the assessed sites in the 2024 report.
tq: Identify the exact percentage rather than approximating the reported figure.
sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following correctly represents the order of the States with the highest reported occurrence of fluoride above 1.5 mg/L in groundwater?
x: The reported order is Rajasthan first, followed by Haryana and Karnataka.
tq: Test a ranked comparison by preserving the order of the three entries.
sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

s: Which polluted river stretch in Andhra Pradesh was identified near Rajamahendravaram?
x: The Godavari near Rajamahendravaram was identified among the polluted river stretches in Andhra Pradesh.
tq: Use the place-river association to avoid swapping neighbouring river systems.
sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

s: Kolleru Lake is under severe pollution stress primarily because:
o: It receives untreated sewage from Delhi and Haryana
Its lake bed was converted into aquaculture ponds and it receives farm runoff
It is affected only by sea-water intrusion
Its water is diverted exclusively for thermal power generation
x: Kolleru’s severe eutrophication is linked to conversion of the lake bed into aquaculture ponds and the inflow of farm runoff.
tq: Link the environmental condition with its stated local causes.
sec: AP water bodies under pollution stress  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following places or activities is associated with pollution stress in Andhra Pradesh water bodies?
1. Godavari and Krishna stretches near cities
2. Effluents from Pharma City in Visakhapatnam
3. Tanneries and paper mills
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three are identified sources or locations associated with pollution stress in Andhra Pradesh water bodies.
tq: Use the all-inclusive option when each listed local source is supported.
sec: AP water bodies under pollution stress  [APPSC]

s: At Rajamahendravaram, the municipal corporation discharges approximately how much sewage through the Nalla Channel before drawing drinking water downstream?
x: The municipal corporation discharges 29.6 MLD of sewage through the Nalla Channel and draws 65 MLD of drinking water just downstream.
tq: Distinguish the sewage-discharge figure from the downstream drinking-water withdrawal.
sec: AP water bodies under pollution stress  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Godavari at Rajamahendravaram:
1. The municipal corporation draws 65 MLD of drinking water downstream of the Nalla Channel discharge.
2. The river stretch was reported to be unfit for drinking or bathing.
3. Nitrate concentration was reported as 119.6 mg/L.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The reported stretch was unfit for drinking or bathing, had nitrate at 119.6 mg/L, and the city drew 65 MLD downstream of the discharge.
tq: Verify several independent measurements and use conditions together rather than relying on one figure.
sec: AP water bodies under pollution stress  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following were identified as the main polluters associated with the Godavari at Rajamahendravaram?
o: Thermal plants and urban water-supply reservoirs
Pharma City and the Krishna Delta canal
Andhra Paper Ltd. and the Nalla Channel
Only aquaculture ponds in Kolleru Lake
x: Andhra Paper Ltd. and the Nalla Channel were identified as the main polluters. The Andhra Paper Ltd. discharge was reported at 31,934 KLD.
tq: Match the water body with the locally identified polluting sources.
sec: AP water bodies under pollution stress  [APPSC]

s: What proportion of urban sewage is treated in India according to the cited estimate?
x: Only about 28% of urban sewage is treated, while about 72% is discharged untreated.
tq: Distinguish the treated share from its untreated complement.
sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes a sequencing batch reactor (SBR)?
o: It is a membrane-only process designed exclusively for drinking-water desalination
It treats sewage continuously in separate tanks without biological treatment
It uses only activated carbon and no biological process
It treats sewage in batches in a single tank
x: An SBR carries out treatment in batches within one tank, integrating the sequential stages of the treatment process.
tq: Discriminate between SBR and MBR by focusing on batch operation versus membrane filtration.
sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

s: A membrane bioreactor (MBR) is best described as a system that:
o: Stores untreated sewage until natural dilution occurs
Combines biological treatment with membrane filtration for high-quality reuse
Treats sewage through evaporation without biological treatment
Uses only coarse screening for removal of floating matter
x: An MBR combines biological treatment with membrane filtration and can produce water suitable for high-quality reuse.
tq: Use the defining technology in the term rather than confusing it with ordinary activated-sludge treatment.
sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following technologies are associated with sewage treatment plants evaluated or used in the cited context?
1. Activated sludge
2. Membrane bioreactors
3. Activated-carbon polishing
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Activated sludge, membrane bioreactors and activated-carbon polishing are all recognised sewage-treatment technologies in the cited context.
tq: Check whether each listed technology belongs to the treatment chain before selecting the combination.
sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

s: Under the Hybrid Annuity Model for Namami Gange projects, what proportion of payments is linked to 15 years of operation and maintenance?
x: The Hybrid Annuity Model links 60% of payments to 15 years of operation and maintenance.
tq: Identify the contractual percentage and its associated time period together.
sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

s: The Hybrid Annuity Model projects under Namami Gange are intended to treat approximately:
x: The HAM projects under Namami Gange are intended to treat 6,255 MLD of sewage.
tq: Use digit placement carefully when distinguishing project capacities.
sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following correctly describes the urban sewage-treatment gap?
o: Piped sewerage reaches 28% of urban households, plants run at 72% capacity and 33% is treated.
Piped sewerage reaches 64% of urban households, plants run at 33% capacity and 72% is treated.
Piped sewerage reaches 72% of urban households, plants run at 28% capacity and 64% is treated.
Piped sewerage reaches 33% of urban households, plants run at 64% capacity and about 28% of urban sewage is treated.
x: The reported gap consists of piped sewerage access for only 33% of urban households, plant utilisation at 64% capacity and treatment of about 28% of urban sewage.
tq: Keep the three percentages attached to their correct indicators instead of interchanging them.
sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following statements about AMRUT 2.0 is correct?
o: It was launched in 2022 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti and covers only river navigation.
It was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and covers sewerage and water supply.
It was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Finance and covers only industrial effluent.
It was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Environment and covers only solid waste.
x: AMRUT 2.0 was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and covers sewerage and water supply.
tq: Apply the ministry-year-subject triad to avoid swapping authorities.
sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

s: AMRUT 2.0 mandates reuse of what proportion of treated urban wastewater?
x: AMRUT 2.0 mandates reuse of 20% of treated urban wastewater.
tq: Distinguish the mandated reuse target from sewerage-coverage and treatment percentages.
sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

s: Under the stated safe-reuse framework, thermal power plants located within what distance of a sewage treatment plant must use treated wastewater?
x: Thermal plants located within 50 km of a sewage treatment plant must use treated wastewater under the stated framework.
tq: Identify the distance threshold linked to the mandatory reuse requirement.
sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

s: The relaxation of the BOD discharge limit from 10 mg/L to 30 mg/L was criticised primarily because it:
o: Permits a higher concentration of organic pollution in discharged effluent
Reduces the permissible BOD limit by two-thirds
Applies only to drinking-water treatment plants
Requires all effluent to contain exactly 30 mg/L of BOD
x: Raising the limit from 10 mg/L to 30 mg/L permits a higher BOD concentration in discharged effluent, which attracted criticism.
tq: Infer the environmental effect of a reversed regulatory trend—an increased permissible limit.
sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

s: The major arsenic-affected belt in India is associated primarily with which region?
o: Malwa plateau of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
Deccan lava plateau of Maharashtra and Telangana
Western coastal plains of Kerala and Karnataka
Ganga-Brahmaputra plains, particularly West Bengal, Bihar and Assam
x: The principal arsenic belt lies in the Ganga-Brahmaputra plains, especially West Bengal, Bihar and Assam, and extends into Bangladesh.
tq: Use the geographical-belt clue and distinguish arsenic regions from fluoride and uranium regions.
sec: Groundwater contamination - arsenic, fluoride, uranium, nitrate  [other exams]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding groundwater contamination in India:
1. Arsenic contamination is associated with the Ganga-Brahmaputra plains.
2. Uranium contamination above 30 ppb has been reported in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
3. Nitrate contamination above 45 mg/L is reported in 56% of districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The reported arsenic belt is in the Ganga-Brahmaputra plains, uranium above 30 ppb has been found in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana among other states, and 56% of districts exceed the nitrate level of 45 mg/L.
tq: Check each statement against its contaminant-specific region or threshold before selecting the coded combination.
sec: Groundwater contamination - arsenic, fluoride, uranium, nitrate  [other exams]

s: The principal source of widespread nitrate contamination in groundwater is
x: Nitrate contamination is mainly attributed to fertiliser use, and 56% of districts reportedly exceed 45 mg/L.
tq: Identify the source-effect relationship rather than confusing nitrate with industrial or mining contaminants.
sec: Groundwater contamination - arsenic, fluoride, uranium, nitrate  [other exams]

s:
With reference to fluoride contamination of groundwater, consider the following statements:
1. Fluoride above 1.5 mg/L was reported at 9.04% of sites.
2. Rajasthan recorded the highest incidence, followed by Haryana and Karnataka.
3. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are also seriously affected.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The reported fluoride exceedance was 9.04% of sites, with Rajasthan followed by Haryana and Karnataka, while Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are also badly affected.
tq: Separate the national ranking from the additional regional observation before choosing the combination.
sec: Groundwater contamination - arsenic, fluoride, uranium, nitrate  [other exams]

s: The Nalgonda technique for fluoride removal uses which combination of substances?
o: Ferric chloride, ammonia and silica gel
x: The Nalgonda technique uses alum, lime and bleaching powder for fluoride removal.
tq: Test the exact composition of a named treatment technique rather than its general purpose.
sec: Groundwater contamination - arsenic, fluoride, uranium, nitrate  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nitrate — mainly caused by river tourism
Arsenic — Western Ghats as the principal belt
x: Uranium contamination is associated with the Malwa region of Punjab. The other statements use incorrect regions, causes or absolute wording.
tq: Find the correctly matched contaminant-region pair while rejecting absolute and swapped associations.
sec: Groundwater contamination - arsenic, fluoride, uranium, nitrate  [other exams]

s: According to the 2025 groundwater assessment for Andhra Pradesh, which statement is correct?
o: Uranium above 30 ppb was absent from Andhra Pradesh.
Residual sodium carbonate exceeded the permissible limit in exactly 56% of samples.
No widespread groundwater contamination was reported in the State.
Residual sodium carbonate exceeded the permissible limit in 26.87% of samples.
x: The assessment reported widespread contamination in Andhra Pradesh, with residual sodium carbonate exceeding limits in 26.87% of samples. Nitrate, iron and fluoride alerts were also reported.
tq: Match the precise percentage to the correct State-level groundwater finding.
sec: Groundwater contamination - arsenic, fluoride, uranium, nitrate  [other exams]

s: Which of the following correctly represents the BIS acceptable and permissible limits for fluoride in drinking water?
x: Under BIS IS 10500, fluoride has an acceptable limit of 1.0 mg/L and a permissible limit of 1.5 mg/L.
tq: Distinguish the acceptable limit from the higher permissible limit in a standards table.

s:
Consider the following statements about drinking-water standards:
1. The WHO guideline for fluoride is 1.5 mg/L.
2. The BIS limit for nitrate is 45 mg/L.
3. The WHO limit for nitrate is 50 mg/L.
4. The BIS and WHO arsenic limits are both 0.01 mg/L.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct. The stated fluoride, nitrate and arsenic limits correspond to the BIS and WHO standards listed.
tq: Read each standard independently and watch for the swapped BIS-WHO nitrate values.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its drinking-water standard?
x: The BIS iron limit is 0.3 mg/L, whereas no WHO value is specified in the given standards table. The uranium values are 0.03 mg/L under BIS and 30 µg/L under WHO.
tq: Locate the deliberately supplied standard where the source table gives no value.

s: A Common Effluent Treatment Plant is primarily intended to serve
o: Only large dams and irrigation projects
x: A CETP is a shared treatment facility established for clusters of small-scale industries.
tq: Use the institutional-purpose clue to distinguish a shared industrial facility from domestic or ecological infrastructure.

s: Which of the following statements regarding effluent management in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: The State has no CETP for industrial clusters.
The State runs nine CETPs and directs industries towards Zero Liquid Discharge.
Zero Liquid Discharge is required only for municipal sewage plants.
The State permits unrestricted discharge of non-biodegradable effluents.
x: Andhra Pradesh runs nine CETPs, has banned discharge of non-biodegradable effluent, and has directed industries towards Zero Liquid Discharge.
tq: Reject the reversed regulatory statement and identify the combined State-specific fact.

s: The principal treatment action of activated carbon in effluent management is
o: Adsorption of organics, colour, odour and pesticides
Removal of suspended sand exclusively through sedimentation
Conversion of nitrate into atmospheric nitrogen only
Increasing the electrical conductivity of water
x: Activated carbon works mainly through adsorption and can remove organic pollutants, colour, odour and pesticides.

s: Tiruppur textile cluster is cited as an example of
o: Fluoride defluoridation by the Nalgonda technique

tq: Associate the named industrial cluster with the specific effluent-management model.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Non-point source — identifiable factory discharge pipe
x: Industrial effluent pipes and sewage outfalls are point sources because they discharge from identifiable outlets. Agricultural and urban runoff are non-point sources.
tq: Use the identifiable-outlet test to distinguish point from non-point pollution sources.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sewage outfalls are point sources of water pollution.
2. Agricultural runoff is a non-point source.
3. Urban runoff is a non-point source.
4. Only about 28–30% of urban sewage is treated.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct. Sewage outfalls are identifiable point sources, while agricultural and urban runoff are diffuse sources; only about 28–30% of urban sewage is treated.
tq: Combine source classification with the quantitative treatment-coverage fact.

s: Sand mining in river channels commonly leads to
o: Removal of all faecal coliform from the river
Reduced turbidity and restoration of river beds
Increased turbidity and degradation of river beds
Increased dissolved oxygen through natural aeration only
x: Sand mining raises turbidity and degrades river beds, thereby damaging riverine conditions.
tq: Match the human activity with its direct physical impact on river systems.

s:
Arrange the following developments in the correct chronological order:
A. National Ganga Council replaced the National Ganga River Basin Authority
B. Central Ganga Authority was established
C. National Ganga River Basin Authority was established
D. National Mission for Clean Ganga was registered as a society
x: The correct sequence is Central Ganga Authority (1985), National Ganga River Basin Authority (2009), NMCG (2011), and National Ganga Council (2016).
tq: Fix the earliest and latest institutions first, then place the 2009 and 2011 bodies between them.

s: Which body was established in 1985 and chaired by the Prime Minister to run the Ganga Action Plan?
x: The Central Ganga Authority was established in 1985, chaired by the Prime Minister, and ran the Ganga Action Plan.
tq: Match the institution with its founding year, chairperson and programme responsibility.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Mission for Clean Ganga?
o: It replaced the National Ganga Council in 2016.
It is chaired by district magistrates at the district level.
It was established in 1985 as the body that ran the Ganga Action Plan.
It was registered as a society in 2011 and served as the implementing arm of the NGRBA.
x: NMCG was registered as a society in 2011 and functioned as the implementing arm of the National Ganga River Basin Authority.
tq: Distinguish the implementing agency from the earlier authority and later council.

s: The legal basis for the present Ganga authorities is the
o: River Ganga (Rejuvenation, Protection and Management) Authorities Order, 2016
x: The legal base is the River Ganga (Rejuvenation, Protection and Management) Authorities Order, 2016, notified on 7 October 2016.
tq: Test the exact official title and year instead of accepting a broadly related environmental law.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the present five-tier structure for Ganga governance from top to bottom?
o: National Ganga Council → Empowered Task Force → NMCG → State Ganga Committees → District Ganga Committees
NMCG → National Ganga Council → District Ganga Committees → State Ganga Committees → Empowered Task Force
National Ganga Council → NMCG → Parliament → State Ganga Committees → District Ganga Committees
Empowered Task Force → National Ganga Council → NMCG → District Ganga Committees → State Ganga Committees
x: The five tiers are National Ganga Council, Empowered Task Force, NMCG, State Ganga Committees and District Ganga Committees.
tq: Start with the apex body and trace the administrative hierarchy downward.

s: The Empowered Task Force in the five-tier Ganga governance structure is associated with the
o: Prime Minister only as district-level chair
Director General of the Wildlife Institute of India
x: The Empowered Task Force is headed by or associated with the Jal Shakti Minister, while the National Ganga Council is chaired by the Prime Minister and district committees involve District Magistrates.
tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish levels of authority.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched with CPCB Class A water quality?
o: Outdoor bathing; total coliform not more than 500 MPN/100 ml
Wildlife and fisheries; free ammonia not more than 1.2 mg/L
Drinking after disinfection without conventional treatment; total coliform not more than 50 MPN/100 ml
Irrigation; dissolved oxygen not less than 4 mg/L
x: Class A is meant for drinking water after disinfection without conventional treatment, with total coliform not exceeding 50 MPN/100 ml.
tq: Match the class with its best use and the corresponding coliform criterion.
sec: CPCB designated best-use water quality classes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s:
Consider the following statements about CPCB designated best-use classes:
1. Class B is intended for outdoor bathing.
2. Class C is intended for drinking after conventional treatment and disinfection.
3. Class D is intended for wildlife and fisheries.
4. Class E is intended for irrigation, industrial cooling and waste disposal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements correctly identify the designated best uses of Classes B, C, D and E.
tq: Read the best-use column as a progression of water-quality applications.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the CPCB water-quality class?
o: Class D — dissolved oxygen at least 6 mg/L
Class A — dissolved oxygen at least 6 mg/L
Class C — dissolved oxygen at least 4 mg/L
Class B — dissolved oxygen at least 5 mg/L
x: Class D requires dissolved oxygen of at least 4 mg/L, not 6 mg/L. Class A, B and C require at least 6, 5 and 4 mg/L respectively.
tq: Compare the dissolved-oxygen thresholds sequentially and identify the wrongly raised value.

s: The BOD limit for CPCB Class A water is
x: Class A has a BOD limit of not more than 2 mg/L. Classes B and C have a limit of 3 mg/L, while Class D uses a free-ammonia criterion.
tq: Separate the BOD values of Classes A, B and C from the free-ammonia criterion of Class D.

s:
Which of the following statements regarding Classes D and E is correct?
1. Class D specifies free ammonia up to 1.2 mg/L.
2. Class E is governed by limits for electrical conductivity, SAR and boron.
3. Class E has a prescribed dissolved-oxygen value of at least 4 mg/L.
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Class D specifies free ammonia up to 1.2 mg/L, while Class E uses electrical conductivity, SAR and boron limits; no dissolved-oxygen value is specified for Class E.
tq: Find the exception in the parameter column instead of transferring Class D values to Class E.

s: The Yamuna Action Plan was launched in 1993 mainly for
o: Control of sewage and industrial pollution in the Delhi stretch of the Yamuna
Creation of the National Ganga Council
Development of dolphin safaris on the Ganga
x: The Yamuna Action Plan began in 1993 and focused mainly on sewage and industrial pollution control in the Delhi stretch.
tq: Match the action plan with its river, year and principal intervention.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the National Lake Conservation Plan and NPCA?
o: The National Lake Conservation Plan began in 2001 and was merged with the wetlands programme into NPCA in 2013.
The National Lake Conservation Plan began in 1993 and was merged with the Ganga Action Plan in 2016.
NPCA was created in 1985 by merging the Yamuna Action Plan with the National Ganga Council.
The National Lake Conservation Plan exclusively concerns industrial effluent from Tiruppur.
x: The National Lake Conservation Plan began in 2001 and was merged with the wetlands programme to form NPCA in 2013.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Krishna River conservation — Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
Yamuna Action Plan — principal programme for Malwa uranium remediation
x: The Yamuna Action Plan concerns sewage and industrial pollution control in the Delhi stretch of the Yamuna, not uranium remediation in Malwa.
tq: Reject the unrelated contaminant-region association and retain the conservation-programme matches.

s: Arth Ganga is primarily associated with
o: Exclusive regulation of groundwater fluoride in Rajasthan
Only the construction of conventional sewage treatment plants
A river-linked economy including natural farming, river tourism, treated-water reuse and artisan livelihoods
Replacement of all State Ganga Committees by district bodies
x: Arth Ganga promotes a river-linked economy through natural farming, river tourism such as dolphin safaris, treated-water reuse and support for artisans.
tq: Identify the broad developmental approach from the cluster of linked activities.

s: JALAJ livelihood centres are associated with the collaboration between
o: NMCG and the Wildlife Institute of India
Central Ganga Authority and the World Bank exclusively
National Lake Conservation Plan and the Yamuna Action Plan
CPCB and the World Health Organization

tq: Match the named initiative with its implementing institutional partnership.

o: Ganga Praharis — trained local volunteers for river biodiversity
Ganga Utsav — trained local volunteers for biodiversity
Arth Ganga — replacement of all sewage treatment plants

tq: Discriminate among similarly named Ganga initiatives by their distinct functions.

s: Ganga Gram, introduced in 2016, focuses on
o: Urban sewage outfalls in Delhi only
Industrial textile clusters in Tamil Nadu
x: Ganga Gram was introduced in 2016 for riverside villages.

s: Which statement best describes the major pollution and treatment-capacity concern in the Ganga system?
o: The river has no significant biological contamination because treatment capacity exceeds demand everywhere.
The main problem is only fluoride, while all STPs have identical utilisation levels.
High faecal coliform is a major problem; Haridwar STPs are overloaded whereas Devprayag facilities are under-used.
Devprayag STPs are overloaded and Haridwar facilities are under-used.
x: High faecal coliform is identified as the main Ganga problem, and there is a capacity mismatch between overloaded Haridwar STPs and under-used Devprayag facilities.
tq: Compare the two locations carefully and avoid reversing the capacity relationship.

s: The National Fluorosis Day workshop referred to in the context of water-quality concerns in India is scheduled for which date?
x: The National Fluorosis Day workshop is scheduled for 9 September 2026.

s: Which institution’s 2025 assessment was associated with flagging Andhra Pradesh in relation to groundwater concerns?

tq: Identify the correct institutional authority rather than a neighbouring environmental body.

o: Steel plants, textile mills, sugar factories and oil refineries
Fertiliser plants, automobile units, ports and food-processing units
Pharma City at Visakhapatnam, tanneries, paper mills and aquaculture
Coal mines, cement plants, thermal stations and shipyards
x: The identified major water-polluting sources in Andhra Pradesh are Pharma City at Visakhapatnam, tanneries, paper mills and aquaculture.

s: The clean-up of which river has been linked with preparations for the 2027 Pushkarams?

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the NMCG order of 10 August 2026:
1. It replaced the total ban on construction across the flood plain.
2. It introduced approval-based rules for areas outside the “active flood plain”.
3. It imposed an absolute construction ban throughout every part of the flood plain.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the order replaced the total ban with approval-based rules outside the active flood plain.
tq: Find the false statement created by reversing an approval-based rule into an absolute prohibition.

s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. NGT held the Varanasi Tent City to have violated norms.
B. The Supreme Court sought the status of encroachments on the Ganga bank.
C. Godavari clean-up was reported in connection with the 2027 Pushkarams.
D. The NMCG issued its order concerning construction in the flood plain.
x: The events occurred in the order: 10 January 2026, 15 March 2026, 27 June 2026 and 10 August 2026.
tq: Anchor the sequence using the earliest and latest dates before placing the middle events.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The National Green Tribunal held that the Varanasi Tent City violated norms.
The Supreme Court directed that the Godavari clean-up be completed after the 2027 Pushkarams.
The NMCG order of 10 August 2026 retained a total ban on all flood-plain construction.
The Supreme Court held the Varanasi Tent City to be compliant with all applicable norms.
x: The National Green Tribunal held on 10 January 2026 that the Varanasi Tent City violated norms.
tq: Separate the authority and finding carefully; the neighbouring bodies and outcomes are swapped in the distractors.

s:
Which of the following criticisms has been associated with the implementation of the Namami Gange Programme?
1. Capacity mismatch
2. Top-down implementation
3. Inadequate river-basin planning
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All three are identified criticisms: capacity mismatch, top-down execution and inadequate attention to river-basin planning.
tq: Recognise the cluster of implementation criticisms rather than treating them as unrelated objections.

s:
Assertion (A): The Godavari has become a focus of river-clean-up measures in Andhra Pradesh before the 2027 Pushkarams.
Reason (R): The Namami Gange model has been applied as a model for the Godavari basin.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true, but the adoption of the Namami Gange model is a related policy development and is not stated as the reason for the timing of the Godavari clean-up before the 2027 Pushkarams.
tq: Distinguish between two related true facts and test whether the reason directly explains the assertion.
